newsitem.title: UK: LVMH'S Arnault to resign from Guinness.
newsitem.headline: LVMH'S Arnault to resign from Guinness.

text.p: Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods group LVMH, has resigned from the board of Guinness Plc to allow him to focus on "promoting his alternative proposal" to Guinness' planned merger between Grand Metropolitan Plc.

The statement from Arnault's advisers BZW said he had made the decision to resign "in the face of the opposition of the board of Guinness". It added that Arnault believed his own plan for a three way merger of the wines and spirits businesses of Guinness, GrandMet and LVMH plus a demerger of their food and brewing units offered "significantly greater value creation for all shareholders."
The LVMH chairman detailed his plans to Guinness and GrandMet last week and was disappointed by the "speed and negativity" of the initial reaction to it, said a spokesman for Arnault's camp.
Arnault believed after this disappointing start, it was unlikely that his plan would be examined objectively.
Guinness and GrandMet were not available for immediate comment.

The two British groups announced their merger plans in May, triggering fierce opposition from LVMH, which is the biggest single shareholder in both groups, holding 14.2 percent of Guinness and 6.4 percent of GrandMet.
If Arnault's plan had been adopted, it would have made LVMH a leading shareholder in the new group with a 35 percent stake.
